flags.why: The killed birds are the ones "in the vicinity of light from 1 to 4 a.m.", so the text ties them to the light.
"...killed" continues "Thrushes in the vicinity of light from 1 to 4 a.m.", so it shares the time. Quote should start at "Starlings, Blackbirds, and Thrushes".
The count "numbers" goes with "numbers struck". "were flying about all night" needs its own round_station observation.
Goes with behaviour struck: "numbers struck" is striking the light, which counts as at_light.
"The burst of severe weather" is the cause of the influx, not a weather report for an observation. Taking it as weather is arguable either way.
This is the seen observation ("11 p.m., Wrens and Whitethroats"). Per Example 1, "five killed" is a separate dead observation (shared count).
Same as 16:count: seen is right for "Wrens and Whitethroats". "five killed" belongs to its own dead observation.
"Oct. 13th and 15th" names two days, not a range. Put 15th in other_dates ("and 15th") or make a separate observation.
North Foreland is listed among the "instances" of "immolating itself against the lanterns".
"one struck the lantern and was killed". struck applies only when killing isn't stated. Quote should run to "was killed".
In the "Linnet, _Linota cannabina_" entry, "invariably mixed with Larks" is about Linnets. Larks are only the company.
The text reads "Sept. 10th", and 1879-09-10 copies it. The checker read 16th on the print, which suggests a 10/16 slip in the transcription. Not confirmed against the scan.
"Oct. 12th, 3 a.m., dense fog, ... thousands of Larks ..., many killed". The time covers the whole entry, and dense fog was already taken from it.
Same as 4: the killed Blackbird is one of the birds "in the vicinity of light".
"Sky Lark" appears in neither the chunk nor the context. "Larks" is in the context ("immigration of Larks"), so copying it is right.
"on fourteen days, going W., ... some striking lantern at night": unclear whether the general "going W." covers the subset that struck.
"as a rule, very early in the morning (4.30 to 9.20 a.m.)" describes the usual passage. The hovering is "on foggy, thick nights", which contrasts with it.
"Titmice seen round lantern amongst the Flycatchers" supports a separate Flycatchers observation. The Titmice need their own ("several"), but this record isn't wrong.
"several" counts the Titmice, not the Flycatchers. No count is given for the Flycatchers.
"Larks and Chaffinches through night, ... probably double this number falling overboard" continues that clause, so it shares the time.
"an occasional bird at the glass" states a vague count, which is allowed, like "a few" or "a".
"always in hazy or rainy weather, generally 'haze and rain'" gives the weather in the chunk, so null is wrong. The exact span to take is open.
"sixty picked up on deck" continues "Larks and Chaffinches through night", so it shares the time.
